🌍 Kamalvandi: Protecting information on Iran’s nuclear sites is highly important

📌 London, IRNA – Spokesperson for the Atomic Energy Organization of Iran (AEOI) Behrouz Kamalvandi has stressed the importance of protecting information about Iranian nuclear facilities, including damaged sites, citing the possibility of further attacks and the International Atomic Energy Agency’s (IAEA) failure to safeguard such information.

“If we do not allow them to visit damaged sites, it is very natural. It is because of war and security issues,” he told IRNA on Wednesday, adding that the United States and Israel are seeking access to information to facilitate further acts of aggression. “In such circumstances, protecting information about nuclear facilities is of particular importance.”
​
Kamalvandi, who is in Vienna to attend the IAEA General Conference, criticized the agency for its failure to protect information about Iran’s nuclear sites.
​
“The Agency has acknowledged that it cannot protect the information. That is why we said that if you cannot protect it, we should not provide you with all the information either,” he said.
​
The Iranian official also criticized IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi for adopting a political approach to Iran’s nuclear program, saying his conduct would lead to increased pressure on Tehran.
​
“We do not trust the Director General unless he is willing to make a fundamental change in his approach. He engages in politics more than professional work, and his statements are political,” Kamalvandi said.
​
He added that the IAEA’s reports, as well as Grossi’s statements and interviews, provide the necessary ammunition for political pressure by European countries, the United States and, in particular, the Israeli regime.
​
“That is why Iran has consistently protested against his conduct,” the official said, adding: “The Director General has sought to place the Agency at the service of the Israeli regime and the United States, which raises doubts about the possibility of any fundamental change in his approach.”
​
IAEA resolution against Iran
​
The IAEA Board of Governors, during its meeting last week, adopted a resolution that would refer Iran’s nuclear case to the UN Security Council. The resolution was drafted by the United States and the E3 countries of Britain, France and Germany.
​
Commenting on the resolution, Kamalvandi said Washington had turned to political tools after failing to achieve its goals through military and economic pressure. He said Washington was seeking resolutions at institutions such as the IAEA and the UN Security Council to compensate for those failures.
​
Iranian nuclear chief’s visa ban
​
Kamalvandi said Austria had bowed to US pressure by preventing Mohammad Eslami, Head of the Atomic Energy Organization of Iran, from attending the IAEA General Conference.
​
He said Eslami had been issued a multiple-entry Schengen visa, but Austria cited anti-Iran resolutions in a note sent to Iran’s embassy one day before the conference.
​
Kamalvandi rejected the justification, saying the resolutions had expired and stressing that the host country was obliged to facilitate the participation of delegations.

🖥 War proved US cannot be legitimate superpower: Army

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iranian Army spokesperson Brigadier General Mohammad Akrami-Nia says the US-Israeli war on Iran demonstrated that the United States cannot appear as a legitimate superpower, arguing that the world is moving toward a “post-American” order.

Speaking at a conference on Arabic calligraphy and the Prophet Muhammad’s life in Tehran on Wednesday, Akrami-Nia said the United States has been faced with serious challenges in both its military capabilities and its soft power and morality, resulting in a decline in its standing.
​
He said that more than three decades after the collapse of the bipolar world order, the world is witnessing an accelerating move toward multilateralism and a multipolar order.
​
“In other words, the world is moving from the period of Western and United States hegemony toward a post-American and post-Western order in which countries have greater freedom of action and independence in pursuing their national security and interests,” he said.
​
Akrami-Nia added that the US adopted “aggressive” and “illegal” behavior in an attempt to preserve its hegemony.
​
He cited disregard for international rules, including the prohibition of the use of force and aggression, interference in other countries’ internal affairs, and support for Israel as factors that have weakened Washington’s position in the international system.
